messages.subject: Re: [breedR] test of fixed effects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Roberto.

The short answer is no, there is nothing provided to help in that endeavour.

First, because I don't  think a NHST approach is really helpful or
meaningful in most settings, and I'm not interested in fostering the
common misconceptions around it (i.e. that smaller p indicates stronger
relationship and that statistical significance indicates practical
importance).

Second, because breedR is quite limited (limitation inherited from the
underlying computational libraries) in the specification of contrasts or
alternative parameterizations of the fixed components. Thus, it is not
very useful to have the ability of conducting NHST if you have no
control of what exactly to test.

Of course, you are free to manually compute your statistics and perform
any tests you like. I'd be glad to include contributed code after some
revition and validation, if people finds it useful.

Best wishes

        ƒacu.-

messages.subject: Re: progress in multitrait development
messages.body_plain:
I don't know where you are with respect to the joint analysis of multiple traits, but I just heard of the Formula <https://cran.r-project.org/package=Formula> package, which you may find useful.
Tim

Le dimanche 22 mai 2016 14:55:12 UTC+2, ƒacu.- a écrit :
>
> I have just fitted the first multitrait model with breedR! Look:
> > summary(res)
> Formula: cbind(y1, y2) ~ 0 + X + bl
>    Data: testdat
>   AIC  BIC logLik
>  5279 5299  -2636
>
> Variance components:
> $Residual
>       [,1]   [,2]
> [1,] 1.005  3.034
> [2,] 3.034 13.246
>
> Fixed effects:
>            value   s.e.
> X.y1    -0.88948 0.1094
> X.y2     5.35030 0.3972
> bl.y1.a  0.16539 0.0739
> bl.y1.b  0.64511 0.0776
> bl.y1.c -0.56196 0.0797
> bl.y2.a  0.26565 0.2684
> bl.y2.b -2.43762 0.2820
> bl.y2.c  1.22552 0.2895
>
> Admittedly, it is a very simple one ;) with only a couple of fixed effects.
> Still, it should give you a feeling of how it goes.
> Notice the estimated residual full covariance matrix (data was simulated with values 1, 3 and 13).
> Also notice that for each fixed effect you have trait-wise estimates.
>
> All the basic elements are ready for models with any kind of random effect, as well.
> I am now polishing some rough edges concerning the extraction of results (i.e. ranef(), model.matrix(), summary()), etc.
>
> I will need to pause the development for a few weeks now (conferences, and other activities), but I thought you would like to know where we are in this regard which is of interest to many.
>
> I certainly expect to have a fully working basic multitrait (i.e. the General case in the UI specs <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/doc/UI_spec_multitrait.pdf>) before august.
>
> ƒacu.-
> ​

messages.body_plain:
Thank you Tim.

I vaguely remember to have looked at it at some point, but unfortunately
I didn't take any notes, and I don't remember my conclusions with
respect to breedR.

Concerning the progress of the multitrait feature, I am embarrased and
sorry that I haven't finished it yet!! Since september I needed to focus
on applying for other positions, preparing and attending competitive
exams and finnishing some papers (to increase chances!) since my
contract here at INRA ends soon. Nevertheless I am committed to finish
at least this one feature before I leave.

ƒacu.-
